tagline.text: A remote limestone island in Batanes, the Philippines' northernmost frontier

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱3,000~8,000 (transport, lodging and guide included, 1 night from Basco)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Basco Airport (BSO), then boat or plane to Itbayat (Jorge Abad Airport)

children.text: Itbayat is the largest island in the Batanes group and the northernmost inhabited part of the Philippines. It is lightly touristed, so you can see limestone cliffs, caves and traditional stone houses in peace, but plans change easily with the sea and the weather.
Itbayat is the largest island in Batanes, covering about
83km²

with roughly 2,900 residents in the 2024 census. You reach it by crossing the sea north of Batan Island, where Basco is, and it is divided into five barangays. While Sabtang and Batan are famous for green hills and lighthouse photos, Itbayat feels far rougher and quieter.

Most of the coast is high cliffs and the interior is a gently rolling tableland, so there are only a few ports where boats can land. This long isolation has kept much of the Ivatan way of life intact. According to Wikipedia, Austronesian settlers arrived 2,000 to 4,000 years ago, a church and civil government were established in the Spanish era of the 1700s and 1800s, and it became a municipality in 1935.

The sights are Torongan Cave and Hills, Rapang Cliff and its ringing stone, the cliffs of Paganaman port, a white-sand beach said to be formed by an earthquake landslide, and the traditional houses of stone and lime around the villages. If you expect fancy resorts or cafes you will be disappointed, but if you like walking, chatting and living at the island's pace, you will be well rewarded. Rather than packing in many sites, pick one for the morning and one for the afternoon and rest in town the remainder of the day. With so few vehicles, discuss each day's plan with your guide first.

Access is the biggest variable. You can go by boat from Basco, but trips are cancelled when waves are high, and small planes are said to fly only when seats are filled. If you add Itbayat to a Batanes trip, keep a spare day or two in case weather keeps you longer.

Torongan Cave is said to have been a dwelling of the island's earliest inhabitants, and there is a burial ground above it. Wikipedia says it is believed to be where Austronesians from Taiwan first landed. It takes about
45 minutes to 1 hour
on a forest trail from town, and a cool breeze is said to blow inside.

blocks.title: Rapang Cliff and the Ringing Stone

children.text: Rapang Cliff is a preserved natural-park area with a mushroom-shaped rock that rings like a bell when struck. Early settlers are said to have used it to call meetings. It is a long
5–7 hour
round trip through hills and forest from town, so many people start before dawn.

Paganaman is a fishing port beneath the cliffs, and in the late afternoon light slips between the rock walls. A small lagoon of natural rock pools is described at the foot of the nearby cliffs. Keep away from the water's edge when waves are high.
This white-sand beach is said to have been created by an earthquake-triggered landslide. Few tourists come, so it is quiet. Ask your guide that day about the route and sea conditions.
Known as the island's highest point at about
. You can ride up by tricycle, and on a clear day the island's tableland and the sea spread out below. The view deck is sometimes under repair, so check locally.

blocks.title: The Town and Sta. Maria Immaculada Church

children.text: The central barangay of Santa Maria has a plaza, the municipal building and a church said to have been built in 1845. Houses of stone and lime with cogon grass roofs are typical of Ivatan vernacular architecture. It is a pleasant place to stroll slowly.

blocks.title: Komayasakas Cave River and Manoyok Sinkhole

children.text: Komayasakas Cave is where an underground stream runs out to the sea, and Manoyok is a sinkhole about
deep that was explored in 1993. Neither is a developed attraction, so check safety conditions with your guide before going.
Small islands such as Siayan, Di'nem and Mavulis lie off Itbayat. One guide quotes a boat trip to the northern islands at about
a day for a boat of up to 10 people, but that information is old. Boats go only when the weather allows.

items.title: 1 night 2 days
items.subtitle: A taste of the town and the cliffs

children.text: Board the boat to Itbayat at Basco port. Arrive early so your name is added to the passenger manifest.
Arrive at Chinapoliran port, go to your lodging and drop your bags. Ride a tricycle into town.
Walk around the plaza, church and market area, have lunch, then pay the tourist fee and book a guide.
Go to Paganaman port for the cliffside scenery and sunset.
Hike the forest trail to Torongan Cave and Hills.
After lunch, head to the port or airport in time for your boat or plane.
The boat back may be cancelled, so try to book any onward flight from Basco for the day after your return or later.

items.title: 3 nights 4 days
items.subtitle: All the way to Rapang Cliff

children.text: Arrive by boat, stroll the town, visit the church and watch the sunset at Paganaman.
Visit Torongan Cave and Hills and the small lagoon in the morning, then rest or chat with locals in the afternoon.
Set out before dawn to walk to Rapang Cliff and the ringing stone and return to town in the morning. In the afternoon see Kaxobcan Beach and Mt. Karoboban.
Buy souvenirs such as garlic at the town market and take the boat back to Basco.
Some guides note that the Rapang stretch needs a separate guide, so book as soon as you arrive.
Fly from Manila (MNL) to Basco Airport (BSO) in Batanes. Carriers and fares vary by season, so check booking sites.
From Basco, continue to Itbayat by boat or small plane.
Flights in Batanes often change with the weather, so keep spare days before and after your Itbayat plans.
The Itbayat boats are small vessels that leave Basco in the morning (roughly
) and return from Itbayat at roughly
The fare is about
one way and the trip takes about
2–4 hours
; many accounts say there is no service on Sundays (older information).
Trips are cancelled when waves are high. Sign the manifest before boarding and bring a raincoat and a waterproof bag.
Check the operators (M/B Ocean Spirit, M/B Itransa, M/B Veronica and others) and times at Basco port.
Small aircraft such as NorthSky Air are said to link Basco and Jorge Abad Airport in Itbayat, but service is not regular.
The flight takes about
7–15 minutes
and is quoted at about
one way (a 2025 article says about ₱3,000 on a six-seater); flights often run only when seats are filled.
Contact the operator directly before booking to confirm days and seat requirements.
The port is about
2km
from town, and a tricycle costs about
To reach the sights from town, hire a guide's motorbike or a tricycle for the day.
The airport is away from town, so ask about transfers in advance.
Itbayat is directly exposed to the northeast monsoon, so from December to February temperatures drop and seas get rough. This is when boats from Basco are least reliable.
One guide names April to June as the best time to visit and says November to March is cool enough to need a light jacket. Average annual rainfall is reported at about
and humidity is high.

Islanders also decide on the morning itself whether the boat runs, so ask your lodging or the port staff in Basco the day before you leave. Older accounts say seas are calmer around the full moon, but this is not guaranteed.

There are almost no regular hotels on the island; homestays and small lodges are the norm. Older reviews mention places such as Cano's Lodge and Levinda Lodge. It is safest to book lodging and a guide together before arriving, and some places reportedly cut power at night, so ask your lodging. Hosts often help with guide contacts, packed meals and port pickups, so contacting them early makes the trip much smoother.

For meals, use the eateries in the town center or the catering cooperative, and you can ask for a packed lunch on hiking days. Buy water and snacks at the village store beforehand. The island's garlic is said to be famous, so look for it as a souvenir.
Arrive at Basco port well before departure so your name is added to the passenger manifest.
Spray can soak you on the boat, so bring a raincoat, a waterproof bag and seasickness medicine.
On arrival, go straight to the municipal office to check the tourist fee and any required registration, and book a guide.
Rapang Cliff is usually started before dawn. Bring a headlamp and comfortable walking shoes.
Do not drink tap water; buy bottled water.
Mobile coverage is reported to be weak, so download maps and your itinerary beforehand.

Since 15 June 2026 all visitors entering Batanes must pre-register online (or through an accredited operator) before boarding their flight. A fee of about ₱405 has been reported but is not confirmed against an official fee table, so check the provincial portal and your airline before you leave.
Carry plenty of cash in small bills, and assume cards and ATMs will not work on Itbayat.
Weather can halt both boats and planes to Itbayat, and being stranded on the island really happens. Do not schedule this trip right before an international flight.
Cliff edges and rocks reached by waves are very dangerous, so stay within the limits your guide sets.
Caves and sinkholes have no safety equipment, so never enter alone.
Do not collect corals, orchids or other protected species.
Medical facilities are very limited, so bring a basic medicine kit and insurance.
Access is sometimes restricted by government exercises or local conditions, so check the latest announcements.
The boat to Itbayat departs from Basco, which is the island's base. It fits well before or after your Itbayat stay.
A stone-house village south of Batan with scenery quite different from Itbayat. It needs a boat transfer, so plan it as a separate day.
Small islands north of Itbayat that can be reached by boat only when weather allows. Arrange with a local boat owner in advance.
